newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Selfix hits acquisition trail.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Selfix hits acquisition trail.

text.p: As it prepares to close a deal that could triple its annual sales, Selfix Inc is cranking up its acquisition efforts to bring a variety of independent housewares companies under its corporate umbrella.
"Phase one (of a 1995 restructuring) was to get Selfix back on track and we've done that," Chief Executive James Tennant told Reuters. "Phase two is the growth through acquisition strategy."
Tennant expects to complete its purchase of Tamor Plastics Corp of Leominster, Mass., within two weeks.
The deal is expected to add about $80 million to the Chicago-based household products manufacturer's annual sales of about $41 million. Terms were not disclosed.
Tennant said Newell Co, a Freeport, Ill.-based holding company, is a paradigm for the Selfix consolidation strategy.

"I characterize Newell as having put together a string of unmatched pearls because they have everything from pens and pencils to Levelor blinds, " Tennant said. "Selfix's consolidation strategy will be to put a string of matched pearls together.

"Tamor is about as perfect a fit as we could ask for," he said. "Tamor sells to virtually the same customers that we sell to. And the manufacturing process that Tamor uses is injection molding, which is the exact process we use."
Tennant added that Tamor will give Selfix access to office product channels where it previously had little presence, while Selfix will give Tamor home center and food and drug distribution channels.

"We're not going into this transaction looking for any massive consolidation or downsizing," Tennant said. "It's one of those situations where if it's not broke we're not going to fix it and neither of these companies is broke right now."

Tennant said Selfix, which will report earnings for the 1996 fourth quarter and full year on Tuesday, will release preliminary expectations for the combined company sometime soon after the Tamor purchase closes.
Last November, Selfix raised its earnings projections for 1996 to between $0.17 to $0.20 a share. Previously, the company expected earnings of between $0.05 and $0.07 a share.
"The earnings estimate increase is strictly reflective of the continued earnings momentum at Selfix," Tennant said.
In 1995, Selfix posted a loss of $1.11 a share, which included a $0.55 restructuring charge.
Selfix shares were up 1/8 Friday afternoon at 11-1/4.
